objects.definition:
enum class GraphemeBreakProperty : uint8_t {
  OTHER              =  0,
  CR                 =  1,
  LF                 =  2,
  CONTROL            =  3,
  EXTEND             =  4,
  ZWJ                =  5,
  REGIONAL_INDICATOR =  6,
  PREPEND            =  7,
  SPACINGMARK        =  8,
  L                  =  9,
  V                  = 10,
  T                  = 11,
  LV                 = 12,
  LVT                = 13,
  EXTPICT            = 18
};
objects.description: Strongly-typed enum identifying Unicode Grapheme Cluster Break properties for a code point. Values are aligned with update_unicode.py and UAX #29.
Strongly-typed enum for Unicode Indic Conjunct Break properties (per UAX #44). Values match update_unicode.py.
Plain-data structure mirroring a row from the internal Unicode table used to build a CodePoint. Holds string views and small property fields. Not exported; used internally for constructing CodePoint.

Represents a single UTF-8 code point with derived Unicode properties and case/normalization forms. Constructible from a UTF-8 substring representing one code point. Non-copyable, movable. Provides accessors for normalized, folded, swapped case strings, property queries, and ordering by canonical combining class.
Type alias for a sequence of pointers to CodePoint objects, used as the return type of BreakIntoCodePoints.
Exception type thrown when UTF-8 decoding fails. Inherits from std::runtime_error and overrides what().

Represents a single UTF-8 grapheme cluster with Unicode NFD-normalized form, base form (no diacritics), folded-case and swapped-case variants, and flags for base/letter/punctuation/uppercase. Non-copyable, movable. Constructed from a UTF-8 string view of one grapheme; provides comparison and smart matching helpers.
Alias for a sequence of pointers to Character objects, stored in a std::vector. Ownership is not implied; elements are const Character pointers.
Type alias for a std::bitset with 256 bits (one per possible byte value). Used to record which raw byte values are present in a Word's underlying UTF-8 text.

Represents a sequence of UTF-8 characters (extended grapheme clusters). Constructed from an rvalue std::string; provides access to original text, parsed character sequence, length, emptiness, and a byte-presence bitset for fast subset checks. Copy/move/assign/destruct are defaulted as shown; note: public API exposes move construction/assignment, but copy construction/assignment are declared in protected section, effectively making copying from outside the class disallowed. Internal helpers split UTF-8 into CharacterSequence per Unicode grapheme rules and compute bytes present.
Standard library type referenced as a parameter; not defined here and should normally be ignored per instructions. Included here only to note absence of custom definitions in this header.

objects.definition:
// filepath -> identifiers
using FilepathToIdentifiers = HashMap< std::string, std::vector< std::string > >;
objects.description: Type alias for a hash map from file path to a vector of identifier strings discovered in that file.

objects.definition:
// filetype -> (filepath -> identifiers)
using FiletypeIdentifierMap = HashMap< std::string, FilepathToIdentifiers >;
objects.description: Type alias for a hash map from filetype (e.g., language) to another map of file paths to their identifier strings.

Thread-safe class that stores identifiers discovered by the identifier completer, organized by filetype and filepath, and provides query functionality. It owns a map of candidates and references a Repository<Candidate> for storage/lookup. Construction details beyond the default constructor are not present here. Destruction semantics are standard; repository_ is a reference and must outlive this instance.

Forward declaration of the Candidate class within the YouCompleteMe namespace. Only a declaration is present; the class is not defined in this header, so its members and purpose are unknown from this file.

A completion engine that manages an internal IdentifierDatabase and provides APIs to add identifiers (from strings or tag files) and query completion candidates, optionally scoped by filetype. Copy and assignment are disabled; default and two additional constructors are provided. Lifetime/ownership notes: it owns an IdentifierDatabase member by value.

Forward declaration of a Result class within the YouCompleteMe namespace. The actual structure, methods, and purpose are not defined in this header. It is referenced by Candidate::QueryMatchResult to return a match result against a query Word. Details unknown due to missing definition here.

Completion candidate type in YouCompleteMe, derived from Word (defined in Word.h). It stores the original text (via base Word), a case-swapped variant, precomputed word-boundary characters, and a flag indicating if the text is lowercase. Provides a move-only public API (copy operations are declared private with defaulted definitions, effectively making copying inaccessible from outside the class), a clone() that returns a by-value copy, and a QueryMatchResult method that computes a Result for a given query Word. Construction uses an explicit rvalue std::string. Internals are computed via private helper methods. Destruction is defaulted. Ownership: not owned by any specific parent in this header; it owns std::string/CharacterSequence members.

Ranking/score container for a completion Candidate against a query Word within YouCompleteMe. Stores multiple match features (subsequence, prefix, word-boundary matches, sum of match indexes) and provides comparison for sorting and lightweight accessors to candidate text and word-boundary size. Constructors and comparison are declared here; feature computation likely occurs in SetResultFeaturesFromQuery (private). Uses non-owning pointers to Candidate and Word; lifetime of those must outlive Result. Details of Candidate and Word are in Candidate.h and are not defined here.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::CodePoint::CodePoint
functions.description: Constructs a CodePoint from a UTF-8 encoded string that represents exactly one Unicode code point. On construction, it computes and stores normalization, case-folded, case-swapped forms, letter/punctuation/uppercase flags, grapheme break property, combining class, and Indic conjunct break property using the internal Unicode table. Throws on invalid UTF-8 or if the input does not form a single code point.
requirements: Argument code_point must be a valid UTF-8 sequence representing exactly one Unicode code point.
On invalid UTF-8 or decoding error, an exception is thrown (UnicodeDecodeError as declared in this header).
The resulting object must remain alive for any references returned by its accessors (e.g., Normal, FoldedCase, SwappedCase) to remain valid.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::CodePoint::Normal
functions.description: Returns the normalized UTF-8 string for this code point, suitable for equality/comparison where canonically equivalent sequences should match. The returned value is stored within the object.
requirements: The CodePoint object must be successfully constructed.
The returned reference remains valid only while the CodePoint object is alive; do not store beyond the object's lifetime.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::CodePoint::FoldedCase
functions.description: Returns the case-folded UTF-8 string for this code point. For caseless code points, this is identical to the normalized form. Useful for case-insensitive comparisons.
requirements: The CodePoint object must be successfully constructed.
The returned reference must not outlive the CodePoint object.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::CodePoint::SwappedCase
functions.description: Returns the case-swapped UTF-8 string for this code point: lowercase if the code point is uppercase, uppercase if lowercase, otherwise identical to the normalized form for caseless code points.
requirements: The CodePoint object must be successfully constructed.
The returned reference must not outlive the CodePoint object.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::CodePoint::IsLetter
functions.description: Returns true if this code point is classified as a letter according to the Unicode table used by the library; false otherwise.
requirements: The CodePoint object must be successfully constructed.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::CodePoint::IsPunctuation
functions.description: Returns true if this code point is classified as punctuation according to the Unicode table used by the library; false otherwise.
requirements: The CodePoint object must be successfully constructed.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::CodePoint::IsUppercase
functions.description: Returns true if this code point is in uppercase. Returns false if it has no uppercase version or is not uppercase.
requirements: The CodePoint object must be successfully constructed.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::CodePoint::GetGraphemeBreakProperty
functions.description: Returns the GraphemeBreakProperty of this code point, used to segment text into extended grapheme clusters per Unicode TR29.
requirements: The CodePoint object must be successfully constructed.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::CodePoint::CombiningClass
functions.description: Returns the Canonical Combining Class (CCC) value for this code point. Can be used to order combining marks according to the Unicode Canonical Ordering algorithm.
requirements: The CodePoint object must be successfully constructed.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::CodePoint::GetIndicConjunctBreakProperty
functions.description: Returns the IndicConjunctBreakProperty of this code point, used for segmentation in Indic scripts as per Unicode TR44.
requirements: The CodePoint object must be successfully constructed.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::BreakIntoCodePoints
functions.description: Splits a UTF-8 encoded string into a sequence of pointers to CodePoint objects, one per decoded Unicode code point. Throws on UTF-8 decoding errors.
requirements: Argument text must be valid UTF-8; on invalid UTF-8 a UnicodeDecodeError is thrown.

Returned CodePoint pointers must be treated as valid only per the function's implementation/ownership semantics (lifetime management is not specified in this header). Callers must avoid dereferencing pointers after their owning storage is destroyed. (Details unknown due to header-only view).

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::UnicodeDecodeError::what
functions.description: Returns a C-string describing the Unicode decoding error. Overrides std::runtime_error::what().
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid for the lifetime of the exception object and must not be freed by the caller.
Noexcept: callers must not expect exceptions from this function.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::Character
functions.description: Constructor for a UTF-8 grapheme-cluster Character. It takes a UTF-8 encoded string representing a single grapheme cluster, normalizes it using NFD, and computes derived representations (base, folded case, swapped case) and properties (letter, punctuation, uppercase). Use this to construct Character instances from user text before comparisons or matching.
requirements: The input 'character' should be a UTF-8 encoded string corresponding to a single grapheme cluster (inferred from class comment).
Behavior for empty or multi-grapheme inputs is unknown (not documented).
No lifetime requirement on 'character' beyond the call since data are stored internally.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::Normal
functions.description: Returns the NFD-normalized UTF-8 representation of the character. Use when you need the canonical decomposed form used internally for comparisons.
requirements: The Character object must outlive any use of the returned reference.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::Base
functions.description: Returns the 'base' form of the character (normalized then stripped to a base representation used for base comparisons). Intended for accent/diacritic-insensitive comparisons.
requirements: The Character object must outlive any use of the returned reference.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::FoldedCase
functions.description: Returns the case-folded version of the normalized character, suitable for case-insensitive comparisons.
requirements: The Character object must outlive any use of the returned reference.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::SwappedCase
functions.description: Returns the case-swapped version of the normalized character (upper-to-lower or lower-to-upper), useful for certain matching strategies.
requirements: The Character object must outlive any use of the returned reference.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::IsBase
functions.description: Indicates whether this character is a base character (i.e., without combining marks) according to the class's normalization logic.
requirements: Requires a properly constructed Character instance.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::IsLetter
functions.description: Returns true if the character is classified as a letter.
requirements: Requires a properly constructed Character instance.
Exact classification criteria are not documented; inferred from name.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::IsPunctuation
functions.description: Returns true if the character is classified as punctuation.
requirements: Requires a properly constructed Character instance.
Exact classification criteria are not documented; inferred from name.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::IsUppercase
functions.description: Returns true if the character is uppercase.
requirements: Requires a properly constructed Character instance.
Exact uppercase determination method is not documented; inferred from name.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::operator==
functions.description: Equality operator comparing Characters by their normalized (NFD) representation. Use for canonical equality of grapheme clusters after normalization.
requirements: Both this and 'other' must be valid Character objects constructed from UTF-8 input.
Compares normalized forms; two visually different inputs that normalize to the same NFD will compare equal.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::EqualsBase
functions.description: Returns true if the two Characters share the same base representation (diacritic-insensitive match). Useful for matching e with é, etc.
requirements: Both this and 'other' must be valid Character objects.
Comparison ignores diacritics/combining marks as defined by the class’s base computation.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::EqualsIgnoreCase
functions.description: Case-insensitive equality based on case-folded representations of the normalized characters.
requirements: Both this and 'other' must be valid Character objects.
Case folding specifics are not documented; behavior follows the class’s folded_case computation.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Character::MatchesSmart
functions.description: Performs 'smart' matching that combines base and case logic: if this is a base character, it matches same base and, if uppercase, only uppercase; if this is lowercase, it matches case-insensitive; otherwise requires exact normalized match. Examples: e matches e, é, E, É; E matches E, É; é matches é, É; É matches É.
requirements: Both this and 'other' must be valid Character objects constructed via the constructor.
Matching semantics are as described in the header comments; relies on is_base_, is_uppercase_, base, and folded-case comparisons.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::NormalizeInput
functions.description: Normalizes an input UTF-8 string for use with Character-based matching. Intended to bring raw text into the same normalization scheme (likely NFD) used internally. Exact normalization form and additional processing are not documented and are inferred from context.
requirements: Input 'text' should be UTF-8 encoded (inferred from class context).
Exact normalization details and error handling are unknown (not documented).
Returned string owns its memory; no lifetime constraints beyond usual C++ string usage.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Word::Word
functions.description: Constructs a Word from an rvalue UTF-8 encoded std::string. The constructor parses the text into user-perceived characters (grapheme clusters) following Unicode TR29 Grapheme Cluster Boundary Rules and precomputes a byte-presence bitset for fast containment checks. Use by passing an rvalue (e.g., std::move(str)).
requirements: Parameter text must contain UTF-8 encoded data; malformed UTF-8 may lead to unspecified behavior during character segmentation.
Ownership of the underlying string is moved into the Word; the caller must not rely on the previous contents of the moved-from std::string after the call.
Construction performs parsing; very large inputs may have a non-trivial cost.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Word::Word
functions.description: Copy-constructs a Word from another Word. This member is declared protected in the class, effectively preventing copying from outside the class but allowing it within class/derived contexts. Performs a memberwise copy of the underlying text, character sequence, and byte bitset.
requirements: Callable only where access to the protected constructor is permitted (inside YouCompleteMe::Word or a friend/derived class).
Source object other must be a valid, initialized Word.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Word::operator=
functions.description: Copy-assigns this Word from another Word. Declared protected; not callable from outside the class (except by friends/derived classes). Performs memberwise copy of text, character sequence, and byte bitset.
requirements: Callable only where access to the protected assignment operator is permitted (inside YouCompleteMe::Word or a friend/derived class).
Both this and other must be valid, initialized Word instances.
Self-assignment is permitted by defaulted semantics.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Word::~Word
functions.description: Destroys the Word, releasing its owned resources. Defaulted destructor with no special behavior.
requirements: The Word object must not be used after destruction.
If references to Text() or Characters() were retained elsewhere, they become invalid once the Word is destroyed.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Word::Characters
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the sequence of grapheme clusters parsed from the original UTF-8 text.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the referenced Word object remains alive.
The returned sequence is const; callers must not attempt to modify it.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Word::Text
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the original UTF-8 text used to construct the Word.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the referenced Word object remains alive.
The returned string is const; callers must not attempt to modify it.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Word::Length
functions.description: Returns the number of grapheme clusters (user-perceived characters) in the Word.
requirements: None beyond having a valid, initialized Word.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Word::ContainsBytes
functions.description: Returns true if this Word’s underlying byte set contains all byte values that appear in other. This is a fast, byte-level containment check and does not compare grapheme clusters or code points.
requirements: Parameter other must be a valid Word.
The result is based on raw byte presence, not textual semantics; callers must not interpret true as substring or character containment.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Word::IsEmpty
functions.description: Returns true if the Word contains zero grapheme clusters.
requirements: None beyond having a valid, initialized Word.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::ExtractIdentifiersFromTagsFile
functions.description: Parses a tags file located at the given filesystem path and returns a FiletypeIdentifierMap of identifiers discovered in that file. Intended for loading identifiers (per filetype) from an existing "tags" database into ycmd. The exact tags file format and mapping semantics are not documented here; based on the name, it is expected to consume a standard tags-style file. Returns the populated map on success.
requirements: path_to_tag_file must designate a path to a tags file on disk.
path_to_tag_file should reference a readable, existing regular file; otherwise parsing will fail (exact failure mode unknown).
The file contents must be in the tags format expected by ycmd; specific format details are unknown from this header.
Thread-safety and exception behavior are not specified in this header; callers should be prepared for potential exceptions from filesystem/I/O operations.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierDatabase::IdentifierDatabase
functions.description: Constructs a thread-safe identifier database used by the identifier completer to track identifiers per filetype and filepath. Initializes internal repositories and synchronization primitives. Typical usage: create one instance and share it across threads that add identifiers and query results.
requirements: May be constructed on any thread.
Object is thread-safe for concurrent use of its public methods after construction.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierDatabase::AddSingleIdentifier
functions.signature: void YouCompleteMe::IdentifierDatabase::AddSingleIdentifier(std::string&& new_candidate, std::string&& filetype, std::string&& filepath)
functions.description: Adds a single identifier (candidate) to the database associated with the given filetype and filepath. Intended to incrementally record identifiers discovered in a specific file.
requirements: Caller must provide a valid filetype string naming the language or filetype; exact accepted values are not specified.
Caller must provide a valid filepath string designating the source file whose identifiers are being recorded; format is not specified.
new_candidate should be a valid identifier string; behavior for empty strings is unspecified.
Parameters are rvalue references; pass temporaries or std::move existing strings to avoid copies.
Safe to call concurrently with other public methods on the same IdentifierDatabase instance.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierDatabase::RecreateIdentifiers
functions.description: Replaces the entire database contents with the provided mapping from filetype to (filepath -> list of identifier strings). Use this to rebuild the in-memory index from a precomputed snapshot.
requirements: The provided map should contain filetype keys mapping to per-filepath lists of identifier strings; no further constraints are documented.
Parameter is an rvalue reference; pass a temporary or std::move to transfer ownership efficiently.
After the call, previous identifiers stored in the database are discarded/replaced.

Safe to call concurrently; internal synchronization is used, but callers should be aware that simultaneous readers may see either old or new data depending on timing (exact consistency model not documented).

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierDatabase::ClearCandidatesStoredForFile
functions.description: Clears all stored identifiers for the specified file (by filetype and filepath). Intended to drop data for files that were removed or should be reindexed.
requirements: filetype must denote the file's language/type; specific values are not documented.
filepath must denote the target file path; format is not documented.
Parameters are rvalue references; pass temporaries or std::move to avoid copies.
No-op if the file has no stored identifiers (behavior inferred; not explicitly documented).
Safe to call concurrently with other public methods.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierDatabase::ResultsForQueryAndType
functions.signature: std::vector<YouCompleteMe::Result> YouCompleteMe::IdentifierDatabase::ResultsForQueryAndType(std::string&& query, const std::string& filetype, const size_t max_results) const
functions.description: Returns up to max_results completion results matching the given query for the specified filetype. Used by the completer to produce suggestions based on the current query text.
requirements: query should be the identifier prefix or pattern to search for; exact matching semantics are not documented.
filetype constrains the search to that language/type; valid values are not documented.
max_results limits the number of results; may be zero to request no results (behavior when zero is not explicitly documented).
Method is const and thread-safe; it may be called concurrently with other readers and writers.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::IdentifierCompleter
functions.description: Default constructor for an IdentifierCompleter. Initializes an empty identifier completer and its underlying database. Intended for general use when starting with no preloaded candidates. Internal behavior and storage details are unspecified.
requirements: Object must be constructed before any member function is invoked.
No arguments; no special initialization requirements beyond standard construction.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::IdentifierCompleter
functions.description: Constructs an IdentifierCompleter preloaded with the provided list of identifier strings. Useful for seeding the completer with known candidates at creation time. The vector is passed by value (copy or move by caller), so contents are taken from the provided container.
requirements: The candidates vector must contain valid UTF-8/ASCII strings appropriate for identifiers; exact validation is unknown.
Large inputs may impact memory usage and performance; size limits are unknown.
Callers may pass an lvalue or rvalue; the constructor will copy or move accordingly.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::IdentifierCompleter
functions.signature: YCM_EXPORT YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::IdentifierCompleter(std::vector<std::string>&& candidates, std::string&& filetype, std::string&& filepath)
functions.description: Constructs an IdentifierCompleter by moving in a set of identifier candidates along with associated filetype and filepath context. Intended when the initial candidate set is tied to a particular file and language/filetype.
requirements: Callers should pass rvalues (e.g., std::move) for candidates, filetype, and filepath to avoid copies.
filetype should describe the language or file type; exact accepted values are unknown.
filepath should be a valid path string to the file whose identifiers are provided; path validation specifics are unknown.
The rvalue references must refer to valid objects that remain alive until the constructor finishes (standard requirement for passing rvalues).

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::AddSingleIdentifierToDatabase
functions.signature: void YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::AddSingleIdentifierToDatabase(std::string& new_candidate, std::string& filetype, std::string& filepath)
functions.description: Adds one identifier string to the internal identifier database, associating it with the given filetype and filepath. Use to incrementally update the database as new symbols are discovered.
requirements: new_candidate, filetype, and filepath must be valid, initialized std::string objects.
filetype should denote the type of file/language; exact accepted values are unknown.
filepath should be a path to the file that the identifier comes from; path format/validity requirements are unknown.
Function is non-const and requires a valid constructed IdentifierCompleter instance.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::ClearForFileAndAddIdentifiersToDatabase
functions.signature: void YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::ClearForFileAndAddIdentifiersToDatabase(std::vector<std::string>& new_candidates, std::string& filetype, std::string& filepath)
functions.description: Clears all identifiers previously stored for the specified file, then adds the provided list of new identifiers for that file. Useful when reindexing a file after changes.
requirements: new_candidates, filetype, and filepath must be valid, initialized objects.
This operation will remove all prior identifiers associated with the given filepath before adding the new set.
filetype should denote the language/file type; exact accepted values are unknown.
filepath should identify the file whose identifiers are being replaced; specific path format requirements are unknown.
Function is non-const and requires a valid constructed IdentifierCompleter instance.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::AddIdentifiersToDatabaseFromTagFiles
functions.description: Loads identifiers from one or more tag files and adds them to the internal database. Intended to import symbols produced by external tooling (e.g., ctags).
requirements: absolute_paths_to_tag_files must be a valid, initialized vector of strings.
Each element should be an absolute filesystem path to a tag file; the expected tag format and version are unknown.
Callers should ensure the referenced files exist and are readable; error handling behavior on missing/unreadable files is unknown.
Function is non-const and requires a valid constructed IdentifierCompleter instance.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::CandidatesForQuery
functions.signature: YCM_EXPORT std::vector<std::string> YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::CandidatesForQuery(std::string&& query, const size_t max_candidates = 0) const
functions.description: Returns a list of identifier completion candidates that match the given query string. Useful for retrieving suggestions for an input prefix or pattern. The result ordering and matching algorithm are unspecified.
requirements: query must be a valid string rvalue; pass std::move(query_str) or a temporary.
max_candidates is a limit on the number of results; when 0 (the default), it likely indicates no limit, but the exact semantics are unknown.
May be called on a const IdentifierCompleter instance.
Returned vector may be empty if no matches are found.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::CandidatesForQueryAndType
functions.signature: YCM_EXPORT std::vector<std::string> YouCompleteMe::IdentifierCompleter::CandidatesForQueryAndType(std::string& query, const std::string& filetype, const size_t max_candidates = 0) const
functions.description: Returns a list of identifier completion candidates that match the given query string, filtered or influenced by the specified filetype. Useful for language-aware completions. The matching/filtering details and ordering are unspecified.
requirements: query and filetype must be valid, initialized std::string references.
filetype should denote the language/file type; exact accepted values are unknown.
max_candidates limits the number of results; when 0 (the default), it likely indicates no limit, but the exact semantics are unknown.
May be called on a const IdentifierCompleter instance.
Returned vector may be empty if no matches are found.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Candidate::Candidate
functions.description: Constructs a Candidate from the given text, taking ownership by moving from the rvalue std::string. Intended to create a completion candidate with precomputed metadata (case-swapped text, word-boundary characters, lowercase flag).
requirements: Argument text must be an rvalue (will be moved-from); its contents are unspecified after the call.
The constructed Candidate object must be considered valid only after successful construction (no additional initialization steps are documented).

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Candidate::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a copy of this Candidate. Useful when an explicit by-value duplicate is needed despite the class being noncopyable from outside.
requirements: The source object must be a valid, fully constructed Candidate.
Returned object is an independent copy; manage its lifetime separately.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Candidate::~Candidate
functions.description: Destructor for Candidate. Cleans up resources owned by the Candidate instance. Defaulted implementation suggests only standard member cleanup is required.
requirements: Do not access the Candidate or any references returned by its accessors after destruction.
Ensure no external code holds references to internal data (e.g., from CaseSwappedText or WordBoundaryChars) beyond the lifetime of the object.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Candidate::CaseSwappedText
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the candidate text with letter casing swapped (inferred from name and backing member case_swapped_text_). Useful for case-insensitive comparisons or display. Exact transformation rules are not documented.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the Candidate object remains alive and unmodified in a way that might reallocate the underlying storage.
Do not store the reference beyond the Candidate’s lifetime.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Candidate::WordBoundaryChars
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the precomputed sequence of characters corresponding to word boundaries in the candidate text (inferred from name and backing member word_boundary_chars_). Intended to aid in word-boundary-aware matching.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the Candidate object remains alive and unmodified in a way that might reallocate or recompute the underlying storage.
Do not store the reference beyond the Candidate’s lifetime.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Candidate::TextIsLowercase
functions.description: Indicates whether the candidate’s text is entirely lowercase (inferred from name and backing member text_is_lowercase_).
requirements: None beyond passing a valid, fully constructed Candidate instance.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Candidate::QueryMatchResult
functions.description: Computes and returns the match result between this Candidate and the provided query Word. Intended for completion/matching logic to determine how well the candidate matches the query.
requirements: Parameter query must reference a valid, fully initialized Word object whose lifetime extends through the call.
Callers should inspect the returned Result for match details; specific semantics of Result are not documented here.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Result::Result
functions.description: Default-constructs a Result with all scoring flags cleared, counters zeroed, and candidate_/query_ set to nullptr. Intended as a placeholder object that will later be replaced/assigned by a properly initialized Result before use in comparisons or accessors.
requirements: Do not call Text() or NumWordBoundaryChars() on a default-constructed Result (candidate_ is nullptr and will be dereferenced).
Safe to call IsSubsequence() immediately (returns the stored bool, default false).
If assigning into this object, ensure the assigned-from Result is properly initialized.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Result::operator<
functions.description: Defines a strict-weak ordering between Results for sorting and ranking completion candidates. The comparison is based on the Result’s internal scoring features (e.g., subsequence status, prefix match, word-boundary matches, index sums).
requirements: Both this and other should refer to valid Results whose candidate_ (and any data accessed during comparison) remain valid; comparing Results that were default-constructed and never initialized may dereference null pointers depending on implementation.
No side effects are expected; safe to use with std::sort/partial_sort.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Result::Text
functions.description: Returns the candidate’s text string associated with this Result. Use to access the underlying completion text when presenting or further processing a ranked candidate.
requirements: candidate_ must be non-null and point to a valid YouCompleteMe::Candidate.
The referenced Candidate object must outlive the returned reference and this Result.

requirements: T is any type intended to be stored in the repository; the same T must be used consistently by the caller when accessing the repository.

functions.name: YouCompleteMe::Repository::GetElements
functions.description: For each input key string, returns a pointer to a stored T corresponding to that key, creating and caching a new T if the key has not been seen before. The returned vector preserves the order of the input keys. For T=Candidate specifically, keys longer than 80 characters are replaced with an empty string before lookup/creation. Pointers refer to objects owned by the repository and remain valid while the repository lives; they are returned as const to discourage mutation through the pointer.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate valid 7-bit ASCII buffers tailored to exercise YouCompleteMe text logic.
# Goals:
# - Provide UTF-8-safe (ASCII) inputs.
# - Include diverse patterns: identifiers, camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case,
#   mixed case, punctuation boundaries, diacritics not allowed -> stick to ASCII.
# - Cover empty, short, medium, and longer inputs but keep <= 4096 bytes.
# - Provide multiple concatenated strings separated by NUL so FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
#   can consume different segments from the same buffer depending on the fuzzer.
#
# Strategy:
# We assemble a corpus of ASCII patterns known to trigger various paths:
# - pure lowercase/uppercase/TitleCase
# - alternating case to create many word boundaries
# - digits and underscores to change boundary detection
# - punctuation-rich strings
# - long identifier (>80) to exercise repository special-case in comments
# - sequences with repeated characters
# - empty entry
# - space-separated words
# - path-like and tag-like strings
# - random blocks with chosen alphabets
#
# We then shuffle and join them with NULs. Callers can split or read prefixes.

ASCII_PRINTABLE = ''.join(chr(i) for i in range(0x20, 0x7f))
LOW = string.ascii_lowercase
UP = string.ascii_uppercase
DIG = string.digits
PUNC = "!" + "#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\\]^_`{|}~"
WS = " \t\r\n"  # still ASCII


def _rand_ident(r: random.Random, length_range=(1, 32)) -> str:
    n = r.randint(*length_range)
    first = r.choice(LOW + UP + "_")
    rest_alphabet = LOW + UP + DIG + "_"
    return first + ''.join(r.choice(rest_alphabet) for _ in range(max(0, n - 1)))


def _camel_from_tokens(tokens: List[str]) -> str:
    if not tokens:
        return ""
    head = tokens[0].lower()
    tail = [t.capitalize() for t in tokens[1:]]
    return head + ''.join(tail)


def _alt_case(r: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    out = []
    upper = True
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalpha():
            out.append(ch.upper() if upper else ch.lower())
            upper = not upper
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return ''.join(out)


def _repeat_block(s: str, count: int, sep: str = "") -> str:
    return sep.join(s for _ in range(count))


def _make_long_identifier(base: str, min_len: int = 90) -> str:
    if len(base) >= min_len:
        return base
    reps = (min_len + len(base) - 1) // len(base)
    out = (base * reps)[:max(min_len, 81)]
    return out


def _random_block(r: random.Random, alphabet: str, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _mix_words_with_punct(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        kind = r.randint(0, 4)
        if kind == 0:
            parts.append(_rand_ident(r, (1, 8)))
        elif kind == 1:
            parts.append(_rand_ident(r, (1, 3)).upper())
        elif kind == 2:
            parts.append(_rand_ident(r, (1, 3)).lower())
        elif kind == 3:
            parts.append(_random_block(r, DIG, r.randint(1, 4)))
        else:
            parts.append(r.choice(PUNC))
    return ''.join(parts)


def _path_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # POSIX-like path
    segments = [ _rand_ident(r, (1, 6)).lower() for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)) ]
    return "/" + "/".join(segments)


def _tags_like_line(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # ctags-ish: name<TAB>path<TAB>excmd;"\tkind:f
    name = _rand_ident(r, (1, 10))
    path = _path_like(r)
    excmd = r.randint(1, 500)
    kind = r.choice(list(LOW))
    return f"{name}\t{path}\t{excmd};\"\tkind:{kind}"


def _boundary_heavy(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Many uppercase transitions and punctuations
    tokens = [_rand_ident(r, (1, 4)) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 7))]
    camel = _camel_from_tokens(tokens)
    snake = '_'.join(tokens)
    kebab = '-'.join(tokens)
    return camel + ' ' + snake + ' ' + kebab


def _space_separated(r: random.Random) -> str:
    words = [_rand_ident(r, (1, 6)) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 9))]
    return ' '.join(words)


def _punct_block(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return _random_block(r, PUNC, r.randint(5, 20))


def _digits_and_letters(r: random.Random) -> str:
    chunks = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 7)):
        chunks.append(_random_block(r, DIG, r.randint(1, 5)))
        chunks.append(_rand_ident(r, (1, 5)))
    return ''.join(chunks)


def _bounded_ascii(s: str, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Ensure 7-bit ASCII and clamp size
    b = s.encode('ascii', 'ignore')[:max_len]
    return b.decode('ascii', 'ignore')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Base patterns
    patterns: List[str] = []

    # Empty
    patterns.append("")

    # Simple identifiers
    patterns.extend([
        "foo",
        "Bar",
        "bazQux",
        "_private_member",
        "HTTPServer",
        "parse_json",
        "toString",
        "URLDecoder",
        "x",
        "Y",
    ])

    # Random identifiers and variants
    for _ in range(8):
        ident = _rand_ident(r, (1, 24))
        patterns.append(ident)
        patterns.append(ident.upper())
        patterns.append(ident.lower())
        patterns.append(_alt_case(r, ident))

    # Boundary-heavy mix
    for _ in range(4):
        patterns.append(_boundary_heavy(r))

    # Snake/Kebab/Camel constructions
    toks = [_rand_ident(r, (1, 6)) for _ in range(5)]
    patterns.extend([
        '_'.join(toks),
        '-'.join(toks),
        _camel_from_tokens(toks),
        _alt_case(r, _camel_from_tokens(toks)),
    ])

    # Punctuation and mixed
    for _ in range(5):
        patterns.append(_punct_block(r))
        patterns.append(_mix_words_with_punct(r))

    # Digits + letters patterns
    for _ in range(4):
        patterns.append(_digits_and_letters(r))

    # Space-separated words
    for _ in range(3):
        patterns.append(_space_separated(r))

    # Path-like and tags-like lines
    for _ in range(3):
        patterns.append(_path_like(r))
        patterns.append(_tags_like_line(r))

    # Long identifier (>80) to trigger repository path mentioned in docs
    long_base = _camel_from_tokens([_rand_ident(r, (3, 6)) for _ in range(6)])
    long_ident = _make_long_identifier(long_base, 100)
    patterns.append(long_ident)

    # Repeated blocks
    patterns.append(_repeat_block("abc", 10))
    patterns.append(_repeat_block("Aa", 20))
    patterns.append(_repeat_block("_", 50))

    # Random ASCII blocks with controlled alphabets
    for _ in range(5):
        patterns.append(_random_block(r, LOW + UP + DIG, r.randint(5, 40)))
        patterns.append(_random_block(r, ASCII_PRINTABLE, r.randint(5, 40)))

    # Ensure all are 7-bit ASCII and bounded
    patterns = [_bounded_ascii(p, 512) for p in patterns]

    # Shuffle to vary order per seed
    r.shuffle(patterns)

    # Join with NUL separators so consumers can take prefixes safely
    # Also prefix with a small random header to provide immediate short inputs
    header_choices = [
        "", "a", "Z", "0", "_", "-", "A_b", "CamelCase", "snake_case", "kebab-case"
    ]
    header = r.choice(header_choices)

    # Compose final buffer; ensure <= 4096 bytes
    sep = "\x00"  # NUL separator
    blob = header + sep + sep.join(patterns)
    blob = blob[:4096]

    return blob.encode('ascii', 'ignore')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets Arbitrary string inputs used by the fuzzer stubs:
# - Repository::GetElements expects several std::string keys, including:
#   * short arbitrary key (<=256 bytes)
#   * duplicate of the first key
#   * explicit empty key
#   * two long keys (>80 bytes), padded with specific characters (X/Y) by stub
#   * another short arbitrary key
# - Lowercase tests a string_view input up to 2048 bytes, asserting ASCII-only
#   lowercasing semantics. Any bytes are allowed, but including a mix of ASCII
#   letters and non-ASCII bytes increases coverage.
# - UnicodeDecodeError constructs from an arbitrary message (<=512 bytes).
#
# We thus produce a single buffer that the harness can split across multiple
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls to provide diverse, valid strings. The buffer encodes
# multiple sections separated by NUL (\x00) delimiters so that successive
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls read distinct segments while remaining valid arbitrary
# strings.
#
# Layout (joined by NUL):
#   [k0][NUL][k_long1_seed][NUL][k_long2_seed][NUL][short6][NUL][lowercase_blob][NUL][error_msg]
#
# Each part is crafted to be interesting:
# - k0: length 1..256, mix of ASCII, digits, punctuation, and some UTF-8.
# - k_long1_seed/k_long2_seed: varied seeds; the stub will pad them to >=90/95.
#   We vary composition to exercise repository coercion (>80 => empty key).
# - short6: another short key like k0 but different content.
# - lowercase_blob: 64..1024 bytes mixing A..Z, a..z, non-ASCII, boundary bytes.
# - error_msg: 0..512 bytes; may be empty to test empty what() handling.
#
# Note: We keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

ASCII_LETTERS = string.ascii_letters
ASCII_DIGITS = string.digits
ASCII_PUNCT = "-_./:+*@#[]{}()!?,;$%&^~|`'\""
WHITES = " \t\r\n"

# Some representative multi-byte UTF-8 code points to include for variety
UTF8_SAMPLES = [
    "é",  # 0xC3 0xA9
    "Ä",  # 0xC3 0x84
    "Ω",  # 0xCE 0xA9
    "Ж",  # 0xD0 0x96
    "汉",  # 0xE6 0xB1 0x89
    "🙂",  # 4-byte emoji
]

# Non-ASCII raw bytes that are not valid UTF-8 starts (to exercise arbitrary byte paths)
NON_ASCII_BYTES = bytes([0x80, 0x81, 0x9F, 0xA0, 0xFF, 0xFE, 0xF5])


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, choices: str, length: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(choices) for _ in range(length))


def _make_short_key(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 256) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Compose with a mix of ASCII classes
    ascii_pool = ASCII_LETTERS + ASCII_DIGITS + ASCII_PUNCT
    ascii_chunk = _rand_choice(rng, ascii_pool, rng.randint(max(1, n // 4), max(1, n // 2)))
    parts.append(ascii_chunk.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    # Optionally add UTF-8 samples
    if n > 8:
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
            parts.append(rng.choice(UTF8_SAMPLES).encode('utf-8'))
    # Fill the rest with random ASCII
    remaining = n - sum(len(p) for p in parts)
    if remaining > 0:
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, ascii_pool, remaining).encode('utf-8'))
    data = b''.join(parts)
    # Ensure max length cap
    return data[:max_len]


def _make_long_seed(rng: random.Random, target_min: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a seed that will be padded by the stub to >= target_min
    # We vary content with sections that include many >80 boundary letters.
    base_len = rng.randint(10, max(10, target_min - 5))
    s = []
    # Start with alternating uppercase/lowercase to exercise lowercase()
    for i in range(base_len // 2):
        s.append(chr(ord('A') + (i % 26)))
        s.append(chr(ord('a') + (i % 26)))
    if base_len % 2:
        s.append(rng.choice(ASCII_LETTERS))
    # Insert some separators and unicode
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        s.append('-')
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        s.append(rng.choice(UTF8_SAMPLES))
    seed = ''.join(s).encode('utf-8')
    return seed


def _make_lowercase_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII uppercase, lowercase, digits, punctuation, whitespace, and raw non-ASCII bytes
    length = rng.randint(64, 1024)
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < length:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.35:
            out.append(ord(rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)))
        elif choice < 0.60:
            out.append(ord(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase)))
        elif choice < 0.70:
            out.append(ord(rng.choice(ASCII_PUNCT)))
        elif choice < 0.78:
            out.append(ord(rng.choice(WHITES)))
        elif choice < 0.88:
            out.append(ord(rng.choice(ASCII_DIGITS)))
        elif choice < 0.95:
            # Add a valid UTF-8 multi-byte sequence
            out.extend(rng.choice(UTF8_SAMPLES).encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            # Insert arbitrary non-ASCII bytes to ensure pass-through behavior
            out.extend(rng.choice(NON_ASCII_BYTES).to_bytes(1, 'big'))
    return bytes(out[:length])


def _make_error_msg(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Could be empty, short, or longer up to 512
    max_len = 512
    mode = rng.randint(0, 3)
    if mode == 0:
        return b""  # empty
    elif mode == 1:
        s = f"Decode error at byte {rng.randint(0, 10000)}: invalid UTF-8 sequence"
        return s.encode('utf-8')[:max_len]
    else:
        # Random mixture
        parts: List[bytes] = []
        # Start with some readable prefix
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, ASCII_LETTERS + ASCII_DIGITS + ' ', rng.randint(10, 40)).encode('utf-8'))
        # Add a few unicode samples
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4)):
            parts.append(rng.choice(UTF8_SAMPLES).encode('utf-8'))
        # Add some arbitrary bytes
        arb = bytearray()
        for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 50)):
            arb.append(rng.randrange(0, 256))
        parts.append(bytes(arb))
        return b''.join(parts)[:max_len]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # k0 and duplicate will be derived by the stub using multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls;
    # we provide enough segments to satisfy all calls with diverse content.
    k0 = _make_short_key(rng)
    k_long1_seed = _make_long_seed(rng, 90)
    k_long2_seed = _make_long_seed(rng, 95)
    k5 = _make_short_key(rng)
    lower_blob = _make_lowercase_blob(rng)
    err = _make_error_msg(rng)

    segments = [k0, k_long1_seed, k_long2_seed, k5, lower_blob, err]

    # Join segments with NUL separators so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR() can take the next slice.
    # Keep total size under 4096.
    buf = b"\x00".join(segments)
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: ASCII text file. The stub will:
# - Request a filename (FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME) where it will write content produced from FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# - It maps each byte of FUZZ_PARAM_STR into printable ASCII 0x20..0x7E and truncates to 1024 bytes
# - Then calls ReadUtf8File on that path
# Our job: Provide an initial interesting buffer (bytes) that FUZZ_PARAM_STR will read from.
# Strategy: Generate varied ASCII-like content patterns up to 1024 bytes to exercise
# different read sizes and line structures:
# - Empty file
# - Very short lines
# - Many short lines with different line endings (\n, \r\n perceived after mapping; but mapping keeps 0x20..0x7E, so we must include '\n' and '\r'
#   which are below 0x20. However the stub maps bytes via (u % 95) + 32, so output cannot include\n#   or \r. Therefore, include characters that look like separators within printable range, e.g. '|', ',', ';'.
# - Include spaces, tabs become spaces after mapping; tabs are <0x20 so mapping changes them. We'll directly
#   construct within printable range by choosing from 0x20..0x7E equivalently.
# - Include a wide variety of bytes so bytes_present_ style computations in downstream code get exercised if used later.
# - Include long lines, repeated characters, alternating cases, numbers, punctuation, brackets, quotes, etc.
# Note: Since the fuzzer stub remaps bytes, we construct bytes that are already printable ASCII in case the fuzzer
# bypasses mapping in some configuration. Mapping our chosen bytes in 0x20..0x7E space keeps them unchanged.

PRINTABLES = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127))  # 0x20..0x7E

# Some interesting token sets
WORDS = [
    "int", "float", "template", "std", "vector", "Candidate", "Word", "Character",
    "normalize", "FoldedCase", "SwappedCase", "Uppercase", "grapheme", "utf8",
    "Indic", "Result", "Repository", "Identifier", "Add", "Clear", "Query",
]
PUNCT = "._-+/=:;,.|!@#$%^&*()[]{}<>?~`'\""
DIGITS = string.digits
LOW = string.ascii_lowercase
UP = string.ascii_uppercase

def _randPrintable(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(PRINTABLES)

def _make_section(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Build a section mixing identifiers, punctuation, numbers, and case patterns
    parts: List[str] = []
    modes = ["ident", "mix", "punct", "digits", "camel", "snake", "kebab", "brackets", "quoted"]
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < target_len:
        mode = rng.choice(modes)
        if mode == "ident":
            w = rng.choice(WORDS)
            # Randomly change case or duplicate
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                w = w.upper() if rng.random() < 0.5 else w.capitalize()
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                w = w * rng.randint(2, 4)
            parts.append(w)
        elif mode == "mix":
            n = rng.randint(5, 30)
            s = ''.join(rng.choice(LOW + UP + DIGITS) for _ in range(n))
            parts.append(s)
        elif mode == "punct":
            n = rng.randint(3, 16)
            s = ''.join(rng.choice(PUNCT) for _ in range(n))
            parts.append(s)
        elif mode == "digits":
            n = rng.randint(1, 20)
            s = ''.join(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(n))
            parts.append(s)
        elif mode == "camel":
            # CamelCase sequence
            n = rng.randint(2, 6)
            s = ''.join(rng.choice(WORDS).capitalize() for _ in range(n))
            parts.append(s)
        elif mode == "snake":
            n = rng.randint(2, 6)
            s = '_'.join(rng.choice(WORDS).lower() for _ in range(n))
            parts.append(s)
        elif mode == "kebab":
            n = rng.randint(2, 6)
            s = '-'.join(rng.choice(WORDS).lower() for _ in range(n))
            parts.append(s)
        elif mode == "brackets":
            # Include nested brackets content
            core = ''.join(rng.choice(LOW + UP) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 12)))
            s = rng.choice(['(', '[', '{']) + core + rng.choice([')', ']', '}'])
            parts.append(s)
        elif mode == "quoted":
            core = ''.join(rng.choice(LOW + UP + DIGITS + ' _-./') for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 18)))
            q = rng.choice(['"', "'"])
            parts.append(q + core + q)
        # Add separator-like characters that survive mapping
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            parts.append(rng.choice([' ', ' ', ' ', '\t', '|', ',', ';']))
    s = ''.join(parts)
    if len(s) > target_len:
        s = s[:target_len]
    return s

def _build_ascii_file(rng: random.Random, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    # Decide a layout pattern for the file
    pattern = rng.choice([
        "empty", "single_line", "many_lines", "sections", "repeated", "alternating", "longline"
    ])
    if pattern == "empty":
        return b""
    lines: List[str] = []
    if pattern == "single_line":
        line = _make_section(rng, rng.randint(1, min(200, max_bytes)))
        lines = [line]
    elif pattern == "many_lines":
        num = rng.randint(5, 60)
        for _ in range(num):
            line = _make_section(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
            lines.append(line)
    elif pattern == "sections":
        # Structured blocks separated by visible delimiters
        blocks = rng.randint(3, 12)
        for i in range(blocks):
            hdr = f"SECTION_{i}:{_make_section(rng, rng.randint(5, 40))}"
            lines.append(hdr)
            for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
                lines.append(_make_section(rng, rng.randint(0, 60)))
            lines.append("--")
    elif pattern == "repeated":
        token = _make_section(rng, rng.randint(3, 12))
        reps = rng.randint(5, 200)
        body = (token + '|') * reps
        lines = [body]
    elif pattern == "alternating":
        a = "ABCdef123_" + rng.choice([":", ";", "|"])
        b = "ycmdYCMD" + rng.choice(["-", "_", "/"])
        n = rng.randint(50, 800)
        s = ''.join(a if (i % 2 == 0) else b for i in range(n))
        lines = [s]
    elif pattern == "longline":
        # Max length line up to 1024
        lines = [_make_section(rng, rng.randint(512, max_bytes))]

    # Join lines with visible separators since newlines will be preserved as '\n' (0x0A),
    # but the stub maps bytes to 0x20..0x7E; to ensure stable behavior regardless, we avoid relying on newlines.
    # However, including real newlines is still fine if the harness writes ascii directly; they would be remapped.
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    # Ensure size <= max_bytes (1024). If longer, truncate.
    b = text.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > max_bytes:
        b = b[:max_bytes]
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # The stub truncates to 1024 bytes, so generate up to 1024 to keep all content.
    return _build_ascii_file(rng, 1024)
